question: Who has been chosen for the Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development for the year 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Michelle Bachelet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development** for the year **2024** has been awarded to **Michelle Bachelet**, the former President of **Chile**.
 
• She was selected for the prestigious award by an international jury chaired by the former Vice-President of India, **M. Hamid Ansari**.
 
• The award recognizes her "extraordinary contribution" to **human rights**, **gender equality**, and her leadership in **global health** and **poverty alleviation**.
 
• **Michelle Bachelet** made history as the **first female President of Chile**, serving two non-consecutive terms from **2006 to 2010** and **2014 to 2018**.
 
• She was also the inaugural Executive Director of **UN Women** (United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women) and served as the **United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights** from **2018 to 2022**.
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust** noted her lifelong commitment to democratic values and her work in defending the rights of the marginalized and vulnerable populations worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development:**
 
 
• This prestigious award was instituted in **1986** by the **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust** in memory of the former Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is awarded annually to individuals or organizations that have made outstanding contributions toward promoting **international peace**, **disarmament**, and a **new international economic order**.
 
• The prize carries a cash award of **₹25 lakh** and a citation.
 
• Past recipients include world leaders and organizations such as **Mikhail Gorbachev**, **Nelson Mandela**, **UNICEF**, **ISRO**, and **Jimmy Carter**.
 
• In **2023**, the prize was jointly awarded to classical pianist **Daniel Barenboim** and peace activist **Ali Abu Awwad** for their efforts in the **Middle East**.
 
 
 
• **Michelle Bachelet's Background:**
 
 
• Born on **September 29, 1951**, in **Santiago, Chile**, she is a physician by training with a specialization in **Pediatrics** and **Public Health**.
 
• Before her presidency, she served as Chile's **Minister of Health** and **Minister of National Defense**, becoming the first woman in **Latin America** to hold a defense portfolio.
 
• During her tenure as President, she introduced significant **social reforms**, including the expansion of **childcare** and **pension systems** to support the elderly and the poor.
 
• Her leadership during the **2010 earthquake** in Chile and her efforts to rebuild the nation were highly commended internationally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The prize highlights the intersection of **development** and **peace**, emphasizing that sustainable growth is impossible without a stable and equitable global environment.
 
• **Michelle Bachelet** is the **second Chilean** to be associated with high-level international peace recognition in recent years, reinforcing the country's role in global diplomacy.
 
• The selection of a former **UN High Commissioner for Human Rights** underscores the **Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust's** focus on **multilateralism** and the protection of civil liberties in the **21st century**.
 
• The award ceremony typically takes place in **New Delhi**, where the citation is presented by the Chairperson of the Trust.
